Recalibrate the Class Probabilities on Labelled Data

Source: R/recalibrate.R
recalibrate.Rd

soft_lm() requires the class probabilities to be calibrated given the controls. When calibration_check() rejects this, a sample in which the group is observed can be used to recalibrate them. recalibrate() estimates the recalibration map \(E[1\{G = k\} \mid p, X]\) on the labelled sample, checks the recalibrated probabilities out of fold, and recomputes the estimate of the fit with them. It implements the recalibration experiment of Kurbucz (2026, arXiv:2608.11784), which also helps to tell which condition of the estimator fails.

Usage

recalibrate(
  object,
  labelled,
  group,
  probs = NULL,
  interactions = TRUE,
  folds = 5L,
  weights = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'softcats_recalibration'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'softcats_recalibration'
predict(object, newdata, probs = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

[mandatory] (softcats or softcats_recalibration) A fit returned by soft_lm(); for predict(), the result of recalibrate().

labelled

[mandatory] (data.frame) Labelled observations with the controls of the fit, the probabilities and the observed group.

group

[mandatory] (vector or character) Observed category labels in labelled: a column name or a vector. Labels must match the category names of the fit; for a fit with a numeric probability vector use 0/1 or FALSE/TRUE.

probs

[optional] (matrix, data.frame, character, formula or numeric) Probabilities for the labelled observations, or for newdata in predict(), in any form accepted by soft_lm(). NULL reuses the probs specification of the fit, or of the labelled sample in predict(), which works when it was given as column names or a formula (default: NULL).

interactions

[optional] (logical) Whether the map includes the products of the log-odds and the controls (default: TRUE).

folds

[optional] (integer) Number of folds of the labelled sample for the out-of-fold check, at least two (default: 5).

weights

[optional] (numeric, character or formula) Weights of the labelled observations: a vector, a column name of labelled or a one-sided formula (default: NULL).

level

[optional] (numeric) Confidence level of the intervals (default: 0.95).

seed

[optional] (integer) Seed for the folds of the labelled sample. NULL uses the seed of the fit (default: NULL).

x

[mandatory] (softcats_recalibration) Result of recalibrate().

digits

[optional] (integer) Number of significant digits to print (default: 3).

...

[optional] Not used.

newdata

[mandatory] (data.frame) Data with the controls and the probabilities to recalibrate.

Value

recalibrate() returns an object of class softcats_recalibration: a list with estimates (a data frame with columns probabilities, term, estimate, std.error, conf.low and conf.high), calibration (the results of calibration_check() on the labelled sample, original and recalibrated out of fold), spectrum (the score spectra of the estimation sample, original and recalibrated, as returned by score_spectrum()), probs (the recalibrated probabilities of the estimation sample, reference category first), probs_labelled (the out-of-fold recalibrated probabilities of the complete labelled observations), map (the fitted map) and nobs_labelled. predict() returns a matrix of recalibrated probabilities with one row per row of newdata, NA where an input is missing, and the columns in the order of probs. The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

The map is a multinomial logistic regression of the observed group on the log-odds of the probabilities against the reference category, the controls and, with interactions = TRUE, the products of the log-odds and the controls. It is fitted by maximum likelihood with the log-odds as an offset, so that zero coefficients leave the probabilities unchanged. Factor controls enter as dummies, and a level that does not occur in the labelled sample is treated as the first level. Columns that are collinear in the labelled sample are dropped. With few labelled observations, or when the miscalibration does not depend on the controls, interactions = FALSE gives a map with fewer parameters.

The function proceeds in three steps.

  1. The labelled sample is split into folds folds; two folds give the split-half design of Kurbucz (2026). Each fold is recalibrated by the map fitted on the other folds, and calibration_check() is run on the original and on these out-of-fold probabilities, so that the check does not reuse the observations that fitted the map. The maps of the folds are fitted on fewer observations than the final map, so the check is somewhat conservative.

  2. The map fitted on the whole labelled sample recalibrates the probabilities of the estimation sample.

  3. The estimate is recomputed with the recalibrated probabilities, using the folds, the outcome residuals and the learner of the fit. Only the regressions of the probabilities on the controls are refitted, and each starts from the state of the random number generator before the corresponding regression of the fit, so a stochastic learner such as lrn_ranger() draws the same random numbers. The two estimates thus differ only through the recalibration, and update() with the probabilities from predict() and the seed of the fit gives the same estimate.

Recalibration targets calibration given the controls, not the exclusion condition. If the classifier features affect the outcome directly, \(E[Y \mid G, p, X] = \mu(X) + \tau^\top g + d(p, X)\), the estimate converges to \(\tau + M^{-1} E[a\,d]\) with \(M = E[a a^\top]\). A map that moves the probabilities towards their conditional mean given the controls shrinks \(M\) and can amplify this bias. The function therefore reports the eigenvalues of \(M\) and the smallest canonical share before and after recalibration, and the print method notes when recalibration halves the smallest eigenvalue or more. Read together with calibration_check() and exclusion_test(), the change in the estimate indicates which condition fails.

The standard errors after recalibration treat the map as known. They do not include its estimation error and can therefore be too small, especially when the labelled sample is small compared with the estimation sample. The function warns when the labelled sample has fewer than ten observations per parameter of the map.

predict() applies the map fitted on the whole labelled sample to other data, for example to refit the model with update().

References

Kurbucz, M. T. (2026). Coarsening latent-class probabilities: Directional distortion and coverage loss. arXiv preprint. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2608.11784

Cox, D. R. (1958). Two further applications of a model for binary regression. Biometrika, 45(3–4), 562–565. doi:10.1093/biomet/45.3-4.562

See also

calibration_check() for the calibration tests, exclusion_test() for direct effects of the classifier features.

Examples

# Example: Probabilities miscalibrated given the first control
d <- sim_softcats(n = 3000, K = 2, miscalibration = 1.5,
                  labelled_share = 0.3, seed = 8)
fit <- soft_lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = c("prob_A", "prob_B"), data = d,
               learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 8)
rc <- recalibrate(fit, labelled = d[d$labelled, ], group = "group")
rc
#> Recalibration of the class probabilities on 919 labelled observations
#> Map: multinomial logit with 8 parameters on the log-odds, the controls and
#> their products
#> 
#> Calibration on the labelled sample (recalibrated out of fold, 5 folds):
#>  probabilities category    ECE overall p conditional p net of noise
#>       original        B 0.1010    <1e-04        <1e-04       0.0826
#>   recalibrated        B 0.0243     0.906         0.999       0.0000
#> 
#> Information beyond the controls (estimation sample):
#>                      original recalibrated
#> eigenvalue of E[aa']   0.0736       0.0935
#> smallest share         0.5180       0.8600
#> 
#> Estimates (difference from reference category 'A'):
#>  probabilities term estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>       original    B    1.040    0.0697     0.90      1.17
#>   recalibrated    B    0.971    0.0622     0.85      1.09
#> 
#> Standard errors after recalibration treat the map as known.
attr(d, "tau")
#> B 
#> 1 

# Example: Refit with the recalibrated probabilities of all observations
d[, c("rprob_A", "rprob_B")] <- predict(rc, d)
update(fit, probs = c("rprob_A", "rprob_B"))
#> Regression on predicted categories (calibrated soft labels)
#> 
#> Call:
#> soft_lm(formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, probs = c("rprob_A", "rprob_B"), 
#>     data = d, learner = lrn_lm(degree = 3), seed = 8)
#> 
#> Difference from reference category 'A':
#>   Estimate Std. Error  2.5 % 97.5 %
#> B   0.9715    0.06216 0.8496  1.093
#> 
#> Observations: 3000   Cross-fitting: 5 folds, 1 split
#> Learner: lm (degree 3)
